title: 6. Third Council of Constantinople (680)
about: Two wills in Christ: St Maximus and the Garden of Gethsemane.

items.text: In the 7th century a compromise was put forward: Christ has two natures but only one will. St Sophronius of Jerusalem and St Maximus the Confessor resisted; Maximus had his tongue and right hand cut off. In 680–681 the Emperor Constantine IV called a council that vindicated them.
In Gethsemane Christ's human will freely obeys His Father. If He had no human will, our will would not be healed.
The council confessed two natural wills and two energies in Christ, the human will following the divine without resisting. It condemned those who taught one will, including Pope Honorius of Rome.

Because the 5th and 6th councils made no canons, a council met in 692 in the domed hall (Trullo) of the palace and gave 102 canons. The Orthodox Church receives them as part of the 6th Council; Rome does not.

items.father: The canons of the Council in Trullo (Quinisext)

items.text: Our salvation is not God overpowering us but our will freely joined to His, as Christ's human will was. 'Thy will be done' is the prayer of the Garden.

items.father: St John of Damascus on the two wills (Exposition, Book 3)
